record.paper_title: Anomalous transport in the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou model: a review and open problems
record.original_question: What qualitatively new nonequilibrium heat-transport phenomena arise in Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou dynamics when the model is extended to include long-range interactions whose coupling decays as an inverse power of distance, or when disorder and nonlinearity act together in the same system?

evidence.quote: Finally, there is a number of possible new effects that may arise in nonequilibrium FPUT dynamics. We just mention the role of long-range forces, notably coupling which decay as inverse power of the distance [84, 85] and the interplay between disorder and nonlinearity [86, 87].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional chain of N classical particles with displacements q_i and momenta p_i (i = 1, ..., N) governed by the Hamiltonian

  H = Σ_i p_i^2/(2 m_i) + (1/2) Σ_{i ≠ j} K_{ij} V(q_i - q_j) + Σ_i U(q_i),

where V is a nonlinear pair potential of Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou type, e.g. V(x) = x^2/2 + α x^3/3 + β x^4/4. Consider two extensions of the standard nearest-neighbor, homogeneous case:

(a) Long-range couplings: K_{ij} = |i - j|^{-s} for some exponent s > 0 (with appropriate Kac-type rescaling for s ≤ 1), and otherwise homogeneous masses m_i = m, no on-site potential (U = 0).

(b) Disorder plus nonlinearity: nearest-neighbor couplings only, but with random masses m_i (or random on-site potentials U(q_i) = ε_i q_i^2/2) drawn i.i.d. from a non-degenerate distribution, together with α ≠ 0 or β ≠ 0.

Place the chain in a non-equilibrium steady state by coupling the boundary particles to Langevin thermostats at unequal temperatures T_L and T_R, and let J_N denote the time-averaged heat current and κ(N) = J_N N/(T_L - T_R) the finite-size thermal conductivity.

Determine the qualitatively new nonequilibrium heat-transport phenomena that arise in cases (a) and (b) compared with the clean, short-range FPUT chain. Specifically:

1. In case (a), characterize the asymptotic scaling κ(N) ~ N^δ as a function of the decay exponent s, identify the value(s) of s at which transitions between normal (δ = 0), anomalous (0 < δ < 1), and ballistic (δ = 1) transport occur, and describe the structure of the temperature profile and the nonequilibrium current correlations.

2. In case (b), determine whether the combination of disorder and nonlinearity produces normal Fourier conduction (κ(N) tending to a finite limit) for arbitrarily small nonlinearity, or whether anomalous/insulating behavior persists; identify the dependence of κ(N) on the nonlinearity strength and on temperature, and clarify the role of nonlinearity in destroying Anderson localization for energy transport.
artifact.category_tag: Anomalous heat transport in FPUT chains
artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews on anomalous heat transport in low-dimensional systems (2020-2024) discuss long-range FPUT and disorder+nonlinearity as active research directions with no complete picture. Partial results exist (e.g., for long-range harmonic chains with conservative noise, and numerical evidence of size-dependent conductivity in long-range FPUT), but a full classification of regimes and a rigorous understanding of the disorder-nonlinearity interplay for heat transport remain open.

status_evidence.title: Anomalous Heat Transport in Classical Many-Body Systems: Overview and Perspectives
status_evidence.snippet: Review highlights long-range interactions and disorder-nonlinearity interplay as open problems in anomalous transport.
status_evidence.claim: These extensions remain open research directions.

status_evidence.title: Thermal Transport in Long-Range Interacting Harmonic Chains Perturbed by Long-Range Conservative Noise
status_evidence.snippet: Studies anomalous size-scaling of energy flux for long-range harmonic chains with noise, partial results only.
status_evidence.claim: Partial rigorous results exist for long-range chains; the FPUT case remains under investigation.

status_evidence.title: Non-Fourier heat transport in nanosystems
status_evidence.snippet: Recent overview noting incomplete understanding of disorder-plus-nonlinearity heat transport.
status_evidence.claim: The disorder+nonlinearity question for heat transport is acknowledged as open.
